title: Rav Assi bar Abba, Who Reports Rabbi Yochanan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned at Yevamot 39b according to [the Rif’s reading](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Yevamot.13a.5). Hyman suggests that possibly this is what Yuchasin meant in citing Rav Ashi bar Abba reporting Rabbi Yochanan; he considers it undoubtedly his reading in Yevamot there. In [the Gemara’s reading](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.39b.15), Rami [bar] Chama (supplied רמי רב חמא) speaks in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak. The linked [Rosh on Yevamot 4:17:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Yevamot.4.17.1) reads Rami bar Abba, as Hyman reports.[^3]

notes.text: The supplied רמי רב חמא is represented as Rami bar Chama, one person, in this connected transmission. Hyman’s proposed identities, his certainty about the reading and the Assi/Ashi forms remain his claims; the digital evidence does not establish a printing history.

The consulted Vilna text of [Rif Yevamot 13a:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Yevamot.13a.5) gives Rav Assi bar Abba in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, and also records Rami bar Chama in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name as an alternate reading. The latter is the reading at [Yevamot 39b:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.39b.15). Hyman’s report of what Yuchasin read remains his reconstruction.

In this passage the Rosh has Rami bar Abba report in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. The linked Bavli has Rami bar Chama report in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name. The Rif records both the Assi bar Abba form and the alternate Rami bar Chama reading.
